pace_engine.description: All paces derive from one number: the athlete's most recent all-out 5K time in seconds. Until the Jan 20 time trial, use the baseline placeholder and label every pace 'estimated'. When a new 5K time is entered, every session in the plan re-renders.

formulas.riegel_time: T2 = T1 * (D2 / D1) ** 1.06   # D in miles; T1 = five_k_seconds, D1 = 3.10686

tt: all-out: show last 5K pace as the reference, target 'faster than last time'
hills: effort-based: show 'strong effort, tall posture, quick steps' — no pace
strides: effort-based: 'fast but relaxed, 20 seconds' — no pace

formulas.marathon_note: The marathon zone is deliberately conservative for a first marathon (Riegel + 8–15%). Mile 20 is where the race starts.
formulas.treadmill_mph: 60 / (sec_per_mile / 60)   # e.g. 10:00/mi → 6.0 mph. Show the slower end of the zone as the treadmill setting.
formulas.display: Show zones as 'm:ss – m:ss /mi' plus '(treadmill X.X mph)' for easy/long. Round to 5-second increments.

pace_engine.talk_test_fallback: If no 5K time is set, every easy/long run says: 'Talk test. Full sentences. Treadmill 6.0 mph.'

general.rep_in_reserve: Stop every set with 2–3 reps left. If you finish 10 and could do 15, add weight next set. If rep 8 gets ugly, take weight off.
general.first_session: Barbell lifts: empty bar warm-up, then +10–20 lb per set until it feels like work. Dumbbells: a weight you could do 15 of, do 10. Lat pulldown: start around half bodyweight. Err light.
general.progression: Hit the top of the rep range on all sets with reps in reserve → add 5 lb to upper-body lifts, 10 lb to lower-body lifts next session. Can't get 8 on the last set → stay.
general.light_week: Deload / race week: 2 sets per exercise, same weights.
general.soreness: First two weeks back you'll be sore more than expected. Normal. Do the easy run anyway — it helps.
general.log: Write every weight down after every session. Week 1 is calibration.
general.learning: Aakash learns by watching, then copying. Every exercise card gets a 'watch' button that opens a video search for the movement.

nutrition.principle: Three real meals, protein at each, eat in the morning. No numbers, no tracking — unless you want to log.
nutrition.the_loop: Up until 2 → wake at 10 → first meal at 2 PM → dinner at 7 → hungry at midnight → DoorDash → up until 2. Fix the wake time and the rest moves.

breakfast.what: Scrambled eggs + sausage links (the protein) + tater tots + a piece of fruit or a glass of milk
breakfast.when: Within an hour of waking, after the run on run days

lunch_dinner.what: Chicken, rice, corn, avocado — the plate that already works. Keep it.
lunch_dinner.note: Add a second scoop of rice on long-run days and the two days before a race.

late_night.rule: Nothing after 10 PM on Sun–Wed. On Thu–Sat, room food only — never an app.
costco_list: String cheese, beef jerky, turkey sticks
Milk or chocolate milk (best post-run recovery drink in the building)

run_fueling.60_to_75_min: Water. Eat within an hour after.
run_fueling.over_75_min: A gel or chews every 30–40 minutes, starting at ~40 min. Water every 2 miles. Practice this on every long run from March so race day has no surprises.
run_fueling.race_morning: Light breakfast 2–3 hours before: toast + banana, or a bagel + peanut butter. Nothing new. Coffee if you normally have it.
run_fueling.race_week: Carbs at every meal from three days out: rice, pasta, bread, potatoes. Not more food — more carbs.
run_fueling.after_long_runs: Chocolate milk or a real meal within an hour. Then eat normally for the rest of the day, plus a snack.

nutrition.muscle_note: You can't build muscle in a calorie deficit. Lifting three days a week while running means three real meals is the floor, not the ceiling. If the lifts stall for three weeks straight, the fix is usually more food, not more sets.

sleep.bedtime: Flexes. Earlier Sun–Wed nights, later Thu–Sat. Bedtime is almost impossible to force; wake time you can set with an alarm, and after a week or two bedtime drifts earlier on its own.
guardrails: 8:30 is the ceiling, not a suggestion. Sleep till 11 on Saturday and Monday's 7:30 becomes a fight again.
Late nights Thu–Sat are fine as long as the wake time holds. Push the Friday long run to 10 or 11 if needed — don't skip it.
Under 5 hours of sleep: do the easy stuff as planned, swap any hard day for easy.
sleep.reset: The India trip is the free reset: land Nov 25, alarm at 7:30 from Nov 26, hold it through Thanksgiving, on the new clock by Nov 30.
sleep.morning_sequence: Alarm → run (or lift) → shower → McNutt breakfast → class at 11:10. One sequence rebuilds the whole day.
sleep.data: Apple Watch sleep lives in the Health app. Screenshot the weekly chart for Sunday check-ins; Pacer logs hours manually if you want the streak.

rules.name: Pain
rules.text: Dull, general soreness that fades as you warm up: run easy. Sharp pain, one specific spot, or pain that gets worse as you run: stop that run. 2–3 days off running (lifting fine if it doesn't hurt), then test easy. Still there after a week, or you're limping or changing stride: get it looked at (IU Student Health Center). Never run through pain that changes your stride.

rules.name: Sick
rules.text: Above the neck (runny nose, sore throat): easy session fine if you feel like it. Below the neck (chest, fever, body aches): full rest until 24 hours after symptoms clear, then restart easy. Don't make up missed days.

rules.name: Missed days
rules.text: 1–3 days: pick up where the plan is, nothing made up. A whole week: repeat the previous week. Two or more: tell Claude, the next stretch gets rebuilt. Making up missed work is the number one way people get hurt.

rules.name: Bad sleep
rules.text: Under five hours: do the easy stuff as planned, swap any hard day (workout, long run, heavy lower) for easy. The plan bends; it doesn't break.

rules.name: Exam weeks
rules.text: Minimum viable week: two runs and one lift. Never zero. Twenty minutes still counts.

rules.name: The 10-minute rule
rules.text: When you don't want to go: ten minutes. Get out the door, start, and if after ten minutes you still want to stop, stop and it counts. You'll almost never stop. The hard part is the first step, not the workout — and this rule only asks for the first step.

rules.name: Pickleball & basketball
rules.text: They stay. They're also the most likely place you get hurt — rolled ankles especially. If that happens, Rule 1 applies. On lift days, don't play hard right before you lift.

easy_run: If the watch says 7-something, that's the old you. Wave and slow down.
Easy means you could tell someone about DinkIQ the whole way and never lose your breath.
Nothing before 11:10. The morning is yours. Run, shower, eggs, class.
8 laps = 1 mile. 24 laps and you're done. Don't count. Just run.
Section E is a mile and a half from the Arboretum loop. The run starts at the car if you want it to.
The B&O Trail at 6:30 AM is the best place in Hendricks County, and nobody's on it.
You've been a hybrid since 2017. The RAV4 gets it.
Slow runs are the budget. Fast runs are the spending. You know which one comes first.
long_run: Slow is the point. This should feel boring for the first half. Boring is the plan working.
Fuel at 40 minutes, not when you feel bad. By then it's late.
Red River Gorge was the trip you didn't take. Glacier is the one you will. This run is how.
Last October your longest run was a 5K. Look at the number on this card.
Every long run is a deposit. Monumental is the withdrawal.
workout: Comfortably hard: a few words at a time. Not a grunt. Not a speech.
Fast Lane. 23 months of it. Now it's 20 seconds at a time.
This is the one run a week where you look at the watch. Make it count, then forget it.
Hills: tall posture, quick steps, drive the arms. Glacier climbs for five miles. Today you climb for one.
lift: Two years of daily racks don't vanish. The bar remembers you.
Scale it: hit the top of the range with reps to spare, add weight. That's the whole business model.
Shoulders are where 'athletic' lives. Don't skip the lateral raises.
Write it down. Week one is calibration. Week eight is the proof.
Soft hands. Hard data. Log the numbers.
The SRSC at 8 AM is empty. The rack is yours.
rest: Rest is where the adaptation happens. You did the work. Let it land.
Saturday is off. It's not a suggestion. Go watch the Hoosiers.
A rest day with the habits hit still counts. Streak lives.
Nothing to do today except eat three real meals and go to bed on time. Hardest workout of the week for some people.
missed: Tomorrow's a new day. You said it first.
Nothing gets made up. The plan picks up where it is. That's Rule 3, and it's the rule that keeps you healthy.
One missed day is a data point. Two is a pattern. Three is a message to Claude.
morning: 7:30. Alarm, shoes, out. Decide nothing. The decision was made on Nov 5.
McNutt opens before you do. Eggs, sausage, tots, done by 9.
The hard part is the first step. Ten minutes. Then see.
